If APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED or CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is later turned off, refresh flows would call the real OAuth endpoints with the literal string "refresh_token" as the refresh token, permanently bricking those stored credentials with no recovery path. This is a real, specific, diff-grounded design/data-in

judged_text: The 'refresh_token' magic placeholder is a one-way door: any later disabling of the sync endpoint bricks every synced credential with no migration path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, which—when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set—validates only a minimal token shape and then forcibly sets a missing `refresh_token` to the literal string "refresh_token" (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`). Several integrations then persist the parsed token data back into the credential (e.g., Office365 merges the parsed data into `o365AuthCredentials` and updates Prisma, `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`), meaning the real refresh token can be overwritten with this placeholder. If later the sync endpoint/env is disabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` will fall back to the normal provider refresh flow, which requires a real `refresh_token`, but the stored credential may now contain only the placeholder—effectively breaking (“bricking”) those credentials with no recovery path shown in the diff.
